requirement:
R3 — META-MODULE NETWORK VIEW. Show the association structure between protein-motif clusters and RNA (5'UTR/3'UTR) motif clusters, organised into the six meta-modules, carrying motif consensus on nodes and edges; clicking a node or an edge opens a detail panel including annotations. Everything must read as statistical co-occurrence (NPMI + APC, then a four-condition phylogenetic-independence gate), never as demonstrated physical binding.

MEASURED GROUND TRUTH FOR THIS VIEW (re-verified by me, not inherited):
• Graph: 519 nodes / 2,620 gated edges. 201 protein clusters, 318 UTR clusters (251 utr3 + 67 utr5). Edges split 2,024 utr3 / 596 utr5.
• Degree: protein mean 13.03, median 8, p90 35, max 62 (prot_0223, then prot_0085 60, prot_0217 58). UTR mean 8.24, median 5, p90 23, max 39 (utr5_0028, utr5_0090). 5'UTR clusters are hub-enriched: 67 utr5 nodes, median degree 6, vs 251 utr3 nodes, median degree 4.
• Hairball arithmetic: top-10 protein hubs touch 20.5% of edges, top-20 35.9%, top-50 64.1%; top-10 UTR hubs 13.9%, top-50 49.7%. Top-N-by-score subgraphs: 50 edges→50 nodes (min score 0.790), 200→127 (0.558), 500→210 (0.414), 1000→301 (0.312), all 2,620→519 (0.146).
• Bipartite matrix is 201×318 = 63,918 cells with 2,620 filled = 4.10% density — sparse enough that a seriated heatmap is a legitimate primary representation, not a fallback.
• Per-module intra submatrices (P×U cells / edges / density / max degrees): M1 39×67=2,613 / 774 / 0.296 / 44,29 · M2 39×73=2,847 / 409 / 0.144 / 40,19 · M3 62×71=4,402 / 385 / 0.087 / 23,38 · M4 20×53=1,060 / 123 / 0.116 / 16,8 · M5 24×33=792 / 126 / 0.159 / 17,16 · M6 14×18=252 / 43 / 0.171 / 7,8. Every module fits on one laptop screen.
• Cross-module edges: 757 of 2,620 (28.9%), 3 more have an unassigned endpoint (prot_0291×utr5_0013, prot_0108×utr3_0355, prot_0058×utr3_0139). Cross-module mean score 0.2877 vs intra 0.3394.
• The module×module matrix is DIRECTIONAL and asymmetric — protein-module rows × UTR-module columns: M1p→M2u 178 but M2p→M1u 66; M2p→M3u 73 but M3p→M2u 94; M1p→M5u 94 / M5p→M1u 98; M6p→M1u 23 / M1p→M6u 9. Undirected totals M1-M2 244 (mean 0.292), M1-M5 192 (0.325), M2-M3 167 (0.266), M1-M6 32, M1-M3 30, M2-M5 28, M3-M4 22, M5-M6 15, M3-M6 6, M2-M4 5, M2-M6 5, M3-M5 5, M4-M5 4, M1-M4 1, M4-M6 1. A symmetric 6-node meta-graph destroys this asymmetry; the 6×6 heatmap is therefore a MUST, not an alternative.
• Edge attribute ranges over the 2,620: phylo_corrected_score 0.146 / med 0.276 / p90 0.510 / max 1.769; npmi_mip_APC 0.100–0.721 (med 0.142); npmi_raw med 0.220, max 0.731; co_count 10–272 (med 49); n_indep_clades 8–23 (med 13); n_indep_families 9–143 (med 38); clade_concentration 0.108–0.349; frac_co_ZNF 0–0.400 (med 0.015, p90 0.109).
• Node content coverage: 451 of 519 nodes have ≥1 STREME consensus AND a significant PWM; 68 have neither. Only 308 of 519 have ≥1 term at FDR_cluster<0.05 — protein 199/201 but UTR only 109/318; under the authors' triple gate (fdr_cluster & fdr_global & fdr_cmh_cluster all <0.05) it drops to 276/519. Curated labels exist for 37 clusters. Positional histograms are cached for only 142 of 519.
• Consensus honesty: 1,226 consensus rows, coverage median 0.365, and 418 of 1,226 (34%) have coverage < 0.25. utr5_0004's headline CGCCGCCACC has coverage 0.212 over 51 carriers. A logo shown without its coverage is the single most misleading thing this view can do.
• Edge consensus: 1,430 of 2,620 edges have ≥1 consensus-pair row; ZERO of the 757 cross-module edges do. 2,000 of 2,620 have consensus on BOTH endpoints (tier-2 fallback possible); exactly 3 have consensus on neither.
• Carrier genes — VERIFIED: co_count == |transcripts(protein cluster) ∩ transcripts(UTR cluster)| exactly, 800/800 edges tested, computable in 0.02 s from the 541,746 (transcript, cluster) memberships. Cluster-level shared sets: median 64.5, p90 123, max 272. But the consensus-level AND over consensus_presence.npz gives median 23 and returns ZERO for 26 of 500 sampled edges — so consensus-level carriers must never be the default.
• Relaxed tier (passes_phylo OR npmi_mip_APC>0.1) = 7,210 edges over 835 nodes, of which 4,590 fail the gate. 13,385 of the 180,000 pairs have co_count 0.
• UNDER-USED ASSET nobody in the four candidate designs found: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v4_0621/results/corrected_score_matrices.npz holds dense float64 300×600 matrices (npmi_raw, npmi_mip, npmi_weighted, npmi_family, perm_z, perm_p, co, fam_support, frac_co_znf) plus pcl/ucl label arrays. Its `co` reproduces co_count 500/500 and its `npmi_mip` matches the CSV to 5e-5 (the CSV is the rounded copy). This is direct, reshape-free backing for every matrix/heatmap unit. Its sibling results/matrices_cache.npz holds the gene×cluster presence matrices P (18,068×300, int8, sum 137,901) and U (18,068×600, sum 403,544) with the gene id array — the exact provenance of co_count and the fastest source for any carrier-gene set, including sub-threshold pairs.

units.encoding: Solid stroke = at least one consensus-pair row; dashed = cluster-level only. Legend states the counts explicitly.
units.data_source: intermediate/consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz filtered to cl_passes (6,890 rows covering 1,430 cluster pairs)
units.precompute_needed: YES — a per-edge boolean plus the top 3 consensus pairs per covered edge (~3,599 rows)
interactions: legend click → highlight all dashed edges
hover → 'no consensus pair was computed for cross-module edges'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It reproduces the published figure's own encoding, and it makes a systematic data gap visible on the canvas instead of only inside a panel a reader may never open.

units.name: Cross-module edge styling and toggle
units.what_it_shows: The 757 edges (28.9%) that cross module boundaries, on by default, with their count always printed.
units.encoding: Cross-module edges drawn in a lighter stroke with a subtle dash offset; intra-module edges dim to 15% when the reader isolates cross-module, rather than disappearing.
units.data_source: edges joined to the modules.json membership map; 1,860 intra / 757 cross / 3 unassigned
interactions: toggle on/off; turning off prints 'hiding 757 of 2,620 edges (28.9%), including the M5-protein × M1-UTR block the manuscript discusses'
isolate a single module pair
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Six clean bipartite panels would erase nearly a third of the result and the one cross-module observation the paper itself makes (M1-M5, 192 undirected edges, the highest mean score of any cross pair at 0.325).

units.name: Edge hovercard with inline gate sparkline
units.what_it_shows: Both endpoint names, phylo_corrected_score, and the four gate values against their thresholds — before committing to a click.
units.encoding: 260 px card containing four 40-px bullet marks (clade_concentration vs 0.35, n_indep_clades vs 8, npmi_mip_APC vs 0.10, co_count vs 10) plus frac_co_ZNF as a fifth read-only bar.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv columns clade_concentration, n_indep_clades, npmi_mip_APC, co_count, frac_co_ZNF, n_indep_families
interactions: hover; pin with a click
units.library: hand-rolled SVG in an HTML card
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The gate is the entire scientific defence of this graph. Putting it on hover — not two clicks deep — is what stops the view reading as a claim about binding.

units.name: Edge encoding selector with an npmi_raw guard
units.what_it_shows: Lets the reader re-encode edge width by phylo_corrected_score, npmi_mip_APC, co_count or n_indep_clades — and refuses to make npmi_raw the default.
units.encoding: Segmented control; selecting npmi_raw shows an inline warning naming the measured result that 25 of the top 30 raw-NPMI pairs are ZNF clade artifacts, and tints the canvas border.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv; the warning text and counts from results/RAW_top30_annotated.csv verdict column (25 'ZNF clade artifact', 4 'single-clade / weak', 1 'survives')
interactions: switch encoding; the legend ramp and all readouts follow
the warning cannot be permanently dismissed
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Offering raw NPMI without a guard is the single most likely way this portal embarrasses the paper — it regenerates exactly the leaderboard the analysis exists to remove.

units.name: Edge-weight legend ramp with distribution
units.what_it_shows: What edge width means, and where the drawn edges sit in the score distribution.
units.encoding: A width ramp with three labelled reference widths (0.15, 0.28 median, 1.77 max) sitting on top of a 40-bin histogram of the 2,620 scores, so the reader sees that the distribution is heavily right-skewed and that most edges are near the floor.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv phylo_corrected_score
interactions: brush the histogram → filters edges
hover → count in that bin
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A width legend without the distribution invites the reader to assume the thick edges are typical. Median 0.276 against max 1.769 says otherwise.

units.name: Seriated bipartite matrix heatmap (201 × 318)
units.what_it_shows: The same graph as a reorderable adjacency matrix — 63,918 cells, 2,620 filled, 4.10% dense — with module blocks visible as dense diagonal squares and the cross-module edges as off-diagonal spatter.
units.encoding: Rows = protein clusters, columns = UTR clusters, ordered by module then by within-module seriation; cell fill = phylo_corrected_score on a sequential ramp, empty = no gated edge; thin rules delimit the six module blocks; a marginal degree bar on each axis.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv, or preferably the dense float64 matrices in /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v4_0621/results/corrected_score_matrices.npz (pcl 300, ucl 600, npmi_mip, co, fam_support, frac_co_znf — verified: its `co` reproduces co_count for 500/500 edges) sliced to the 201×318 gated submatrix
units.precompute_needed: YES — the row/column seriation order (module blocks + within-block ordering by degree or by a barycentre/cross-count minimisation)
interactions: click a cell → edge inspector
hover a row/column → highlights that node's whole row/column
toggle the encoded quantity (score / npmi_mip_APC / co_count / n_indep_clades / frac_co_ZNF)
reorder by module, degree, or seriation
units.library: canvas 2D for the cells, SVG for the axes and rules
units.prior_art: Bertin's reorderable matrix; matrix view in Cytoscape/Gephi; Ghoniem, Fekete & Castagliola on matrices vs node-link
units.why_it_earns_its_place: At 4.1% density and 519 nodes this is the representation that CANNOT hairball, and it is the only one where a reader can verify that a module is dense and that cross-module edges are not. It also answers the question node-link answers worst — 'is this pair present?' — in constant time.

units.name: Full 300 × 600 grid matrix with gate mask
units.what_it_shows: The entire scored space — 180,000 protein × UTR pairs — with the 2,620 survivors picked out, so the reader sees how small the result is inside what was tested.
units.encoding: Canvas heatmap of npmi_mip_APC over the full grid (distribution min −0.840, median −0.037, p90 0.059, p99 0.183, max 0.875) with the 2,620 gated cells outlined; a second mode masks everything that fails the gate to grey, and a third shows co_count with the 13,385 zero-co-occurrence cells hatched.
units.data_source: results/corrected_score_matrices.npz — dense npmi_raw / npmi_mip / npmi_weighted / npmi_family / perm_z / perm_p / co / fam_support / frac_co_znf, all 300×600 float64, with pcl and ucl label arrays. No reshaping or joining needed.
interactions: zoom into a module block
toggle the encoded matrix
toggle gate mask on/off — the animation of 180,000 → 2,620 is the point
click a cell → pair detail, including sub-threshold pairs marked as such
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This asset exists on disk, fully precomputed, and no candidate design found it. Toggling the gate mask is the most direct possible demonstration that the network is 1.6% of what was tested, and it costs almost nothing to build.

units.name: Module block matrix (6 blocks, zoomable)
units.what_it_shows: A middle zoom between the 6×6 summary and the 201×318 detail: six on-diagonal blocks at their true densities (M1 0.296 down to M3 0.087) plus the off-diagonal cross-module rectangles.
units.encoding: A 6×6 arrangement of sub-matrices with true relative cell sizes, so M1's 39×67 dense block and M6's 14×18 sparse block are visually comparable.
units.data_source: same as R3-27
interactions: click a block → zoom to the full-resolution submatrix
hover → density and edge count
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Density varies 3.4× between modules and that difference is a real result (M1 is a tightly interlocked programme; M3 is a broad, loosely coupled one). Neither the meta graph nor the full matrix shows it directly.

units.name: Bipartite arc diagram (single axis)
units.what_it_shows: All 519 nodes on one horizontal axis ordered by module, with edges as arcs above (protein→UTR) — a linear ordering that makes cross-module edges literally long.
units.encoding: Node ticks coloured by module and shaped by region along the axis; arcs with height ∝ span and opacity ∝ score; cross-module arcs necessarily reach across module boundaries so 28.9% cross-linking becomes a visual fact.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv + the module ordering
units.precompute_needed: YES — the linear node ordering (reuse the min-linear-arrangement in node_select.order_modules(), which was built for exactly this)
interactions: click an arc → edge inspector
hover a tick → its arcs highlight
collapse to module-level arcs
units.prior_art: Wattenberg arc diagrams; hierarchical edge bundling papers
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the one layout where 'this module is self-contained' and 'this module leaks' are the same visual property — arc length. For M4 (only 12 cross edges) versus M1 (353) that contrast is the story.

units.name: Module-flow Sankey
units.what_it_shows: Edges as flow from protein modules (left) through to UTR modules (right), preserving the directional asymmetry (M1p→M2u 178 vs M2p→M1u 66).
units.encoding: Six left nodes (protein side of each module) and six right nodes (UTR side), 36 possible ribbons, width ∝ edge count; ribbons coloured by source module.
units.data_source: the directional 6×6 crosstab of results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv through modules.json
units.precompute_needed: YES — the directional 6×6 matrix
interactions: click a ribbon → those edges in the canvas
hover → count and mean score
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the only representation that separates 'M1 protein motifs pair with M2 UTR motifs' from the reverse, and the asymmetry is 178 versus 66 — far too large to average away.

units.name: Hive plot (three axes: protein / 3'UTR / 5'UTR)
units.what_it_shows: The graph laid out on three fixed axes with nodes positioned by degree, which removes layout arbitrariness entirely and separates the two RNA regions.
units.encoding: Axis 1 protein (201 nodes), axis 2 utr3 (251), axis 3 utr5 (67); radial position ∝ degree; edges as Bezier curves between axes; node colour = module.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv + node region from the cluster prefix
interactions: hover an axis segment → those nodes
toggle axis ordering (degree / module / n_genes)
units.prior_art: Krzywinski et al., hive plots for network comparison
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Hive plots exist precisely to defeat the 'my force layout looks different from yours' problem, and they would make one measured fact immediately visible: 67 5'UTR clusters carry 596 of the 2,620 edges at a higher median degree than the 251 3'UTR clusters. That asymmetry is invisible in every other layout.

units.name: Pair UMAP scatter (interactive Fig 3c)
units.what_it_shows: All 180,000 scored pairs in the published embedding with the 2,620 gated pairs lit — the graph's edges placed in the space of everything that was tested.
units.encoding: Canvas scatter, background pairs at 3 px / 0.15 alpha, gated pairs at 6 px coloured by module or by npmi_mip_APC on a diverging ramp; a fourth colour mode by frac_co_ZNF visually separates the artifact cloud.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v3_0515/07.umap_vis/00.build_embeddings_model_embeddings/results/cca_sweep/cca_winner_umap.npy (180000×2 float32) row-aligned to .../results/embeddings/row_index.csv (row, protein, utr); joined to results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv on (protein, utr) — VERIFIED 2,620/2,620 gated pairs receive coordinates
units.precompute_needed: YES — quantise xy to uint16 over the bounding box (max error 0.000234 units) plus uint16 npmi and uint8 module channels ≈ 0.99 MB gzipped; ALSO record the source path and mtime, because this file lives in the v3 analysis tree that nothing in the v4 pipeline regenerates
interactions: brush/lasso → the selected pairs fill a linked edge table
hover via a quadtree → pair tooltip
click → edge inspector
colour-by switch
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the only view that shows the network's edges in the context of the 177,380 pairs that did not survive, and it is already computed. SVG is not an option at 180,000 points.

units.name: Degree-rank plot (both sides)
units.what_it_shows: The degree distributions of the protein and UTR sides on one log-rank axis, naming the hubs.
units.encoding: Two monotone curves (protein max 62, UTR max 39), the top 5 of each labelled, with median lines at 8 and 5.
units.data_source: degree computed from results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: click a point → focus that node in the canvas
brush a degree band → filter the canvas
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It quantifies the hairball: top-10 protein hubs touch 20.5% of edges, top-50 touch 64.1%. That is the number that justifies the degree-cap control, and showing it makes the control's effect predictable.

units.name: Hierarchical edge bundling toggle
units.what_it_shows: The same edges bundled along the module hierarchy, trading individual-edge readability for legible module-to-module flow.
units.encoding: Radial or column layout with edges routed through module-level control points; bundling strength on a slider from 0 (straight) to 0.95.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv + module membership as the bundling hierarchy
interactions: bundling-strength slider
hovering an edge un-bundles it and its neighbours
units.why_it_earns_its_place: With 757 cross-module edges the straight-line view is at its worst exactly where the interesting cross-links are. Bundling is the standard fix, and it must be a toggle rather than a default because bundling hides individual edges.

units.name: Six-panel small-multiples module grid
units.what_it_shows: All six module bipartite subgraphs at once, at a shared scale, so their sizes and densities are directly comparable.
units.encoding: 2×3 grid of miniature bipartite panels (largest is M3 at 133 nodes / 385 edges), each with its own header stats; identical node-size and edge-width scales across panels.
units.data_source: modules.json membership + the intra-module subsets of results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: click a panel → full-screen module drill-down
shared hover: hovering a node in one panel highlights the same module colour everywhere
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Comparison is a first-class question here ('is M4 like M6?') and small multiples answer it better than any interactive toggle. All six fit on a laptop screen because the largest is 133 nodes.

units.name: Node partner rail (adjacency strip)
units.what_it_shows: For a selected node, all of its partners as a single ordered strip — a one-dimensional replacement for reading edges out of a hairball.
units.encoding: A horizontal rail of partner ticks sorted by phylo_corrected_score, each tick coloured by the partner's module and sized by score; a divider marks where the partner's module changes.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv filtered to the selected node
interactions: click a tick → edge inspector
hover → partner name and score
toggle sort (score / co_count / clades / module)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Median degree is 8 but hubs reach 62; tracing 62 edges out of a node-link diagram is impossible and out of a rail is trivial. It also makes the cross-module fraction of one node's partners immediately visible.

units.name: Ego subgraph focus mode (1-hop / 2-hop)
units.what_it_shows: Only the selected node, its partners, and optionally their partners — the standard escape from a hairball when arriving from R1 or R2 with a specific cluster.
units.encoding: Radial layout with the focus node centred, ring 1 = partners coloured by module, ring 2 = second-degree neighbours at reduced opacity; a node-count readout for each ring.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: 1-hop / 2-hop toggle with counts
re-centre on any node
'return to full graph' preserving the selection
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A reader arriving at ?focus=utr3_0215 wants that node's two partners, not 2,620 edges. This is the primary entry path from R2 and it must not dump the reader into the full canvas.

units.name: Score threshold slider with live node/edge counts
units.what_it_shows: How the graph thins as the edge-weight floor rises, with the surviving counts printed before the reader commits.
units.encoding: Range slider over phylo_corrected_score (0.146–1.769) with the score histogram behind the track and marks at the measured breakpoints: 50 edges→50 nodes at 0.790, 200→127 at 0.558, 500→210 at 0.414, 1000→301 at 0.312.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv phylo_corrected_score
interactions: drag → clientside re-filter, no server round-trip
snap to the labelled top-N presets
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the main anti-hairball control and the counts make its effect predictable. It MUST carry the note that it re-filters edges only and does not re-run Louvain, so module assignments never change under it.

units.name: Strict / suggestive tier toggle
units.what_it_shows: The manuscript's own gate (2,620 edges, 519 nodes) against the labelled relaxed superset (npmi_mip_APC > 0.10 → 7,210 edges, 835 nodes, of which 4,590 fail the gate).
units.encoding: Two-segment control with both counts baked into the labels; relaxed-only edges rendered in a distinct dashed, desaturated style and every one of them carries a 'not phylogenetically independent' tag in tooltips and panels.
units.data_source: results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv columns passes_phylo_filter and npmi_mip_APC (tiers nest exactly: every passing pair has npmi_mip_APC ≥ 0.1001)
units.precompute_needed: YES — the 7,210-row relaxed slice, ~0.74 MB
interactions: toggle; the canvas gains 316 nodes and 4,590 edges, and says so
the relaxed style cannot be turned off while relaxed is active
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 282 of 600 UTR clusters have no strict partner. Relaxing must be the reader's explicit choice, and it must look different — silently filling empty pages by lowering the threshold would misrepresent the paper's central statistical claim.

units.name: Sub-threshold ghost edges
units.what_it_shows: For a selected node, its best non-passing partners drawn as faint ghosts, so 'no partner' is shown as a measured result rather than as missing data.
units.encoding: Dotted, 20%-opacity edges to the top 5 sub-threshold partners, each labelled with the specific condition it failed.
units.data_source: results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (all 180,000 pairs) filtered to the node, sorted by npmi_mip_APC, with passes_phylo_filter False
interactions: toggle per selection, never global
hover → which of the four conditions failed and by how much
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A node with zero partners looks broken. Showing what it almost had, and why that was rejected, converts an empty state into the portal's most educational moment.

units.name: Module isolation toggles
units.what_it_shows: Which modules are on the canvas, with node and edge counts per module.
units.encoding: Six checkboxes in module colours with live counts (M1 106 nodes / 774 intra edges … M6 32 / 43), plus an 'unassigned (6 nodes, 3 edges)' row.
units.data_source: modules.json + results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: check/uncheck; edges with one endpoint hidden are dimmed rather than dropped, with a count of how many that is
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Module is the primary organising variable of the view; without per-module isolation the reader cannot answer any single-module question in the full canvas.

units.name: Region filter (3'UTR / 5'UTR / protein)
units.what_it_shows: Splits the RNA side by region — 251 utr3 nodes carrying 2,024 edges versus 67 utr5 nodes carrying 596.
units.encoding: Three chips with counts; deselecting utr3 leaves a much smaller but hub-heavy 5'UTR graph.
units.data_source: cluster prefix (verified perfectly consistent with region across all 889,215 motif rows)
interactions: toggle; counts update
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 5'UTR and 3'UTR biology are different (Kozak/cap versus ARE/miRNA), and the 5'UTR subgraph is measurably denser per node. Merging them into one 'UTR' side hides that.

units.name: Evidence filters (clades, families, ZNF, co_count)
units.what_it_shows: Filtering by the trust statistics rather than by the composite score.
units.encoding: Four compact range sliders with their own mini-histograms and the gate threshold ticked: n_indep_clades (8–23), n_indep_families (9–143), frac_co_ZNF (0–0.400), co_count (10–272).
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: drag any slider → live edge count
one-click preset 'strongest evidence' (clades ≥ 15 and frac_co_ZNF = 0)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: phylo_corrected_score fuses these into one number; a sceptical reader wants to weight them themselves. Only 11 of 2,620 edges exceed frac_co_ZNF 0.30, and letting a reader discover that by filtering is more convincing than being told.

units.name: Content filters (has logo / has term / has consensus pair)
units.what_it_shows: Restricting the canvas to nodes and edges whose detail panels will actually be populated.
units.encoding: Three chips with counts: 451/519 nodes with a PWM, 308/519 with an FDR<0.05 term, 1,430/2,620 edges with a consensus pair.
units.data_source: the per-node/per-edge completeness flags of R3-18 and R3-22
interactions: toggle; a caption states how much of the graph is being hidden and why
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It lets an impatient reader see only the rich parts, while the counts prevent them mistaking the filtered view for the whole result.

units.name: Degree cap / hub declutter control
units.what_it_shows: Suppresses the highest-degree nodes' edges, which is the most targeted anti-hairball measure available: capping at degree 20 removes the nodes that account for 35.9% (protein) and 25.0% (UTR) of all edges.
units.encoding: A single 'max edges per node' slider (∞ → 5) that keeps each node's top-k edges by score and marks capped nodes with a '+n hidden' badge.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv
interactions: drag; capped nodes badge the hidden count
click a badge → that node's full partner rail
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Score thresholding removes weak edges everywhere; degree capping removes clutter exactly where it is (prot_0223 at 62). Because it hides data, the '+n hidden' badge is mandatory.

units.name: Locate-a-cluster search
units.what_it_shows: Where a named cluster sits, for readers arriving from R1 or R2 with a specific motif in mind.
units.encoding: Search box with typeahead over the 900 cluster ids and their display names; the match pulses and the viewport eases to it.
units.data_source: the per-cluster index (900 rows: cluster, region, module or null, name, counts)
interactions: type-ahead; ?focus= deep link support
a cluster that is in none of the 519 network nodes returns an explicit 'this cluster has no gated partner' result, not an empty search
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 387 of 900 clusters are not in the network at all. Without this, arriving from a motif and finding nothing is indistinguishable from a broken search.

units.name: Declutter preset menu
units.what_it_shows: One-click routes out of the hairball, each labelled with the resulting size.
units.encoding: A menu of presets: 'As published (52 nodes, 113 edges)', 'Top 200 edges (127 nodes)', 'One module', 'Ego of the selected node', 'Matrix instead'.
units.data_source: the measured top-N breakpoints and bipartite_nodes_all6.csv
interactions: click a preset; the active filters appear as dismissable chips so the reader can see what a preset did
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The hairball is not solved by one control but by making the good views one click away. Naming the resulting node counts makes the choice informed.

units.name: Live counts readout
units.what_it_shows: 'Showing 519 of 519 nodes, 2,620 of 2,620 edges (757 cross-module)' — always visible.
units.encoding: One line of monospace counts that changes as any control moves.
units.data_source: the current filter state
interactions: click a count → clears the filters that reduced it
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Every control in this view hides data. A permanent count is the only thing that stops a filtered graph being mistaken for the whole result.

units.name: Active-filter chips
units.what_it_shows: The current filter state as individually dismissable chips, mirrored into the URL.
units.encoding: Pills with an x plus a 'reset all'.
units.data_source: view state
interactions: dismiss one; reset all; the URL updates so a filtered graph is shareable and citable
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A network view that a reader cannot link to from a paper or a reviewer reply is a demo, not a resource.

units.name: Node inspector — identity header
units.what_it_shows: Cluster id, region, module, three-tier name with tier badge, size (n_instances, n_transcripts, n_genes) and degree.
units.encoding: Header block with module and region chips and a stat row.
units.data_source: consensus_scope_clusters.csv, the per-cluster size groupby on identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet (network nodes: n_instances median 906, min 280, max 3,078; n_transcripts median 536, min 52)
interactions: copy id; open the full cluster page (R2); locate in graph
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 'Clicking a node shows details' begins here.

units.name: Node inspector — full sequence logo with statistics
units.what_it_shows: The node's STREME logo at readable size, with E-value, nsites, coverage and carriers printed beneath it.
units.encoding: Information-content logo, bits axis labelled, plus a provenance line: 'STREME v5.5.9, E = 9.2e-14, 394 sites, coverage 0.511 of 566 members, 155 carrier genes'.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl (pwm, w, nsites, evalue, pvalue, consensus, coverage) + consensus_meta.csv (carriers)
interactions: cycle a node's multiple consensus
hover a column → letter probabilities
download the PWM in MEME format and the logo as SVG
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The requirement says 'with motif consensus'. Printing E-value and coverage next to it is what keeps it a measurement rather than a picture.

units.name: Node inspector — consensus repertoire list
units.what_it_shows: All 1–10 consensus of the cluster with coverage and carrier counts, because a cluster is usually not one motif.
units.encoding: Rows of mono consensus + coverage bar + carrier count, sorted by coverage; rows below 0.25 greyed with the warning label.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv (cid, cluster, consensus, coverage, carriers) — 1,226 rows, median 2 per cluster, max 10
interactions: click a row → the logo above switches to that consensus
click carriers → that consensus's carrier gene list
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Showing only the top consensus implies a cluster is one motif. Median 2 and max 10 says otherwise, and the coverage spread across a cluster's own consensus is itself informative.

units.name: Node inspector — full positional histogram
units.what_it_shows: The 20-bin positional distribution at readable size with the median printed and the direction labelled.
units.encoding: Bar chart over relative position 0–1, median tick, axis ends 5'/3' or N/C, n_instances printed.
units.data_source: the recomputed all-900 positional histogram (validated against the 142 in streme_pos_cache_all6.pkl: e.g. utr3_0215 median_pos 0.4441, n=566)
interactions: click a bin → member instances in that band
overlay the region-wide background distribution
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the second Fig 3e glyph and the evidence behind every positional claim the module narratives make.

units.name: Node inspector — enrichment dot plot
units.what_it_shows: The node's enriched annotation terms across all ten sources — the 'annotations' half of the requirement, on the node side.
units.encoding: Dot rows: x = fold (log scale), y = term, size = k, colour = source (InterPro / MobiDB / eCLIP / PAR-CLIP / iCLIP-P / iCLIP-C / miR / ELM / IDPO / SignalP); FDR<0.05 rule drawn; non-significant terms plotted hollow and greyed to the left rather than omitted.
units.data_source: intermediate/cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (260,572 rows covering all 900 clusters; columns cluster, region, source, term, k, n, K, N, fold, p, fdr_cluster, or_mh, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster, display, informative)
units.precompute_needed: YES — de-duplicate on (cluster, source, display) keeping min fdr_cluster, then cap at ~12 rows per cluster (measured: 4,096 rows / 1.27 MB JSON / 0.23 MB gzipped covers every cluster that has a significant term)
interactions: source filter chips
hover → the full 2×2 (k of n cluster genes, K of N=17,831 background)
toggle the authors' triple gate (fdr_cluster & fdr_global & fdr_cmh_cluster all < 0.05), which reduces coverage from 308 to 276 of the 519 nodes
click an InterPro term → interpro.ebi.ac.uk deep link via interpro_entry_map.csv

units.name: Node inspector — no-significant-term state
units.what_it_shows: The honest state for the 211 of 519 network nodes with no FDR<0.05 term — including the manuscript-featured utr5_0090, utr5_0096 and utr3_0215.
units.encoding: Explicit heading 'No term passes FDR<0.05 for this cluster', then the top nominal-p terms greyed and labelled ns, then the instance-frequency fallback.
units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz unfiltered for that cluster
interactions: expand to all rows
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Two thirds of the RNA-side nodes are in this state. An empty panel there would read as a broken portal instead of as a real limit of gene-level enrichment on 17,045–17,831-gene universes.

units.name: Node inspector — instance-level annotation frequency bars
units.what_it_shows: The always-available fallback: what fraction of the cluster's own instances carry each RBP, miRNA or InterPro term (utr3_0215 → LARP4 18, PCBP1 15, PCBP2 14, DDX55 9, UPF1 8).
units.encoding: Ranked horizontal bars with raw count and percentage, headed 'frequency among this cluster's instances — not an enrichment test'.

units.precompute_needed: YES — one groupby per cluster at bake time (measured 1.8 ms live, so either is fine)
interactions: click a bar → member instances carrying it; also seeds an R1 gene search
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the only annotation content that exists for every node, and its header sentence is what prevents a frequency being read as an enrichment.

units.name: Node inspector — partner list with module breakdown
units.what_it_shows: All of a node's partners, sorted by score, with how they split across modules — the fastest way to see that a node is a cross-module bridge.
units.encoding: Table of partner id, name, score, gate values, plus a small stacked bar at the top showing the partner-module composition.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv filtered to the node
interactions: sort by score / co_count / clades
click → edge inspector
filter to cross-module partners only
units.why_it_earns_its_place: For a hub like prot_0223 (62 partners) the module composition is the only summarisable property, and it is exactly the statistic that identifies the M1/M5 bridge nodes.

units.name: Node inspector — aggregated partner protein features
units.what_it_shows: For a UTR node, the union of InterPro/MobiDB/ELM terms across its protein partners — the one-glance answer to 'what kind of protein does this RNA motif travel with'.
units.encoding: Horizontal bars of terms weighted by partner count and fold, each labelled with which partner contributed it.
units.data_source: join of the node's partner list to cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz where region='protein' and fdr_cluster<0.05
units.precompute_needed: YES — a small per-UTR-node rollup
interactions: click a term → the partners carrying it
click a partner → its cluster page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is the literal 'how a motif interacts with protein features' chain, and it is the strong direction: 199 of 201 protein nodes carry a significant term versus 109 of 318 UTR nodes, so the UTR page should lead with its partners' features rather than its own.

units.name: Node inspector — member gene preview
units.what_it_shows: A first look at the genes carrying this cluster's motifs, without leaving the network.
units.encoding: 12 gene chips plus a count and a 'see all' link; chips carrying a module badge where the gene is a module member.
units.data_source: identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet (motif_cluster → sequence_id) joined to motif_full_annotations.parquet gene_symbol; module membership via 03.interacting_modules/module_gene_members/module_gene_index.csv (refseq_ids joins to sequence_id at 100% precision)
interactions: click a gene → the R1 transcript view deep-linked to an instance of this motif
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the shortest path from an abstract node back to a sequence a biologist recognises, which is the handoff that makes R3 useful rather than decorative.

units.name: Edge inspector — facing consensus logos
units.what_it_shows: The protein consensus and the UTR consensus side by side across the association statistics — the bilingual claim made literal, and the requirement's 'edge with motif consensus'.
units.encoding: Two logos mirrored inward with an association bar between them carrying co_count and npmi_mip_APC; each logo captioned with its own coverage and carrier count.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl PWMs for both endpoints; intermediate/consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz (p_consensus, u_consensus, p_coverage, u_coverage, p_carriers, u_carriers, co_count, npmi_mip_APC)
interactions: cycle consensus pairs (mean 4.8 per covered edge, max 50)
click either logo → that cluster's node inspector
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the single image that expresses what this paper found. Everything else in the edge panel is supporting statistics.

units.name: Edge inspector — consensus fallback tier indicator
units.what_it_shows: Which of three tiers of consensus evidence the panel is showing, named in words rather than implied: tier 1 a real consensus pair (1,430 of 2,620 edges), tier 2 each endpoint's own consensus lists (2,000 edges qualify), tier 3 top literal member strings (3 edges need it).
units.encoding: A labelled band above the logos: 'consensus pair' / 'consensus per cluster — no pair was computed' / 'most frequent member sequences'.
units.data_source: consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz → consensus_meta.csv → identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet motifs value_counts
interactions: hover the tier label → why the gap exists (consensus association was only run within modules, so zero of the 757 cross-module edges have a pair)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 45% of edges — including every cross-module edge the manuscript discusses — would otherwise show a visibly weaker panel with no explanation. Naming the tier converts a hole into a stated fact.

units.name: Edge inspector — four-gate bullet gauges
units.what_it_shows: Each of the four gate conditions as a value against its threshold, plus frac_co_ZNF and n_indep_families as read-only evidence.
units.encoding: Six bullet charts: clade_concentration < 0.35 (observed 0.108–0.349), n_indep_clades ≥ 8 (8–23), npmi_mip_APC > 0.10 (0.100–0.721), co_count ≥ 10 (10–272), plus frac_co_ZNF on a 0–0.5 scale (max 0.400, only 11 edges above 0.30) and n_indep_families (9–143). Threshold ticks drawn, pass tinted teal.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv, all six columns
interactions: hover → the condition quoted verbatim from MODULES_REPORT.md and what it controls for
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Bullet charts are the right mark because the question is 'value versus threshold', not 'value versus value'. This is the unit that operationalises the mandatory caveat instead of restating it.

units.name: Edge inspector — full statistics table
units.what_it_shows: Every column of the edge record, auditable and exportable.
units.encoding: Two-column table: co_count, n_indep_families, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF, npmi_raw, npmi_mip_APC, npmi_reweighted, npmi_family, perm_z_withinfamily, perm_p_withinfamily, phylo_corrected_score — with npmi_raw visually de-emphasised and footnoted.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv (15 columns); higher-precision values available from results/corrected_score_matrices.npz, since the CSV is rounded to ~5 decimals (max deviation measured 5e-5)
interactions: copy row; export as CSV/JSON
hover any statistic → its definition
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A reviewer will want the numbers, all of them, in a form they can paste. Hiding npmi_raw entirely would look evasive; de-emphasising it with a footnote is the honest middle.

units.name: Edge inspector — consensus-pair table
units.what_it_shows: Which specific consensus strings carry the cluster-level association, with their own statistics.
units.encoding: Table: p_cid, p_consensus, u_cid, u_consensus, coverages as bars, co_count, npmi_mip_APC, n_indep_clades, and whether the consensus pair itself passes the gate (1,266 of 49,547 rows do).
units.data_source: intermediate/consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz (49,547 rows × 22 columns; 6,890 with cl_passes covering 1,430 cluster pairs; cl_* columns carry the parent cluster statistics on every row)
units.precompute_needed: YES — top 3 per (p_cluster, u_cluster) ≈ 3,599 rows
interactions: sort by npmi_mip_APC
click a row → that consensus pair's carrier genes
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the most scientifically informative drill-down available — it turns 'these two clusters co-occur' into 'these two specific sequences co-occur' — and the data is already computed.

units.name: Edge inspector — shared carrier gene list (cluster resolution)
units.what_it_shows: The actual transcripts carrying both motifs. VERIFIED: this set's size equals co_count exactly (800/800 edges tested), so the list IS the evidence behind the edge, not an approximation of it.
units.encoding: Gene chips with a count header, sorted by the number of instances of either motif; measured set sizes median 64.5, p90 123, max 272, min 15.
units.data_source: intersection of the two clusters' transcript sets from the 541,746 distinct (sequence_id, motif_cluster) pairs in identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet — or equivalently a bitwise AND of the P and U columns in results/matrices_cache.npz (genes 18,068; P 18,068×300 int8; U 18,068×600 int8), which reproduced co_count exactly in my check
units.precompute_needed: OPTIONAL — the intersection is 0.02 s for 800 edges from an in-memory set index, so it can be live; precompute only for a fully static build
interactions: click a gene → the R1 transcript view deep-linked to an instance
export the list as CSV
'send all to the module gene table'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It closes the loop from the network back to sequences and it is exactly reproducible from the published tables — which is precisely the property that makes a portal citable.

units.name: Edge inspector — carrier resolution selector
units.what_it_shows: That 'the genes on this edge' has three different answers, and forces the reader to see which one they are reading: module (thousands), cluster (= co_count, median 64.5), consensus (median 23, and ZERO for 26 of 500 sampled edges).
units.encoding: Three-segment control with the count printed inside each option and a permanent caption naming the active resolution.
units.data_source: module level from module_gene_index.csv; cluster level from the transcript-set intersection above; consensus level from consensus_presence.npz (Pc 18,068×275, Uc 18,068×951, covering only 136 protein and 315 UTR clusters)
interactions: switch resolution; every count and list on the panel updates and relabels
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The consensus-level answer is empty for about 5% of edges whose cluster-level co_count is 15 or more. Defaulting to consensus resolution would make a real edge look like a non-result; making the level explicit is the only safe design.

units.name: Edge inspector — carrier overlap mini-diagram
units.what_it_shows: The three set sizes behind co_count: transcripts with only the protein motif, only the UTR motif, and both.
units.encoding: A three-segment proportional bar (not a Venn — the sets are nested awkwardly and a bar reads more accurately at this size), with the intersection segment highlighted and all three counts printed.
units.data_source: the two cluster transcript sets from identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet or matrices_cache.npz
interactions: hover each segment → count and percentage of each cluster
click the intersection → the carrier list
units.why_it_earns_its_place: co_count alone is uninterpretable without the marginals — 175 shared genes means something very different when the clusters have 445 and 372 genes than when they have 3,000 each. This is what makes NPMI's normalisation legible.

units.name: Edge inspector — rank context
units.what_it_shows: Where this edge sits among the 2,620 gated edges and among all 180,000 scored pairs.
units.encoding: A small histogram of phylo_corrected_score with a marker and a rank label ('#1 of 2,620'), plus a percentile against the full grid.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv and results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv
interactions: hover → percentile
click → the pair explorer with this point selected
units.why_it_earns_its_place: prot_0040 × utr5_0004 at 1.769 is nearly 6.5× the median edge. Without rank context every edge reads as equally strong, which is the classic network-view distortion.

units.name: Edge inspector — clade/family support breakdown
units.what_it_shows: How many independent protein families and deep clades actually support this edge, versus how many genes — the difference the whole paralogy correction rests on.
units.encoding: Three nested bars on a shared log axis: co_count genes (10–272), n_indep_families (9–143), n_indep_clades (8–23), with the collapse from genes to clades made visually literal.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv columns co_count, n_indep_families, n_indep_clades
interactions: hover → the definitions and the 36-protein-class derivation (aa 5-mer TF-IDF → truncated SVD → Louvain)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the per-edge version of the Meff argument (18,068 genes → 2,342 effective) and it is far more persuasive at the point of use than on a methods page.

units.name: Edge inspector — ZNF share bar
units.what_it_shows: What fraction of this edge's co-occurring genes are ZNF paralogs — the specific artifact the pipeline was built to remove.
units.encoding: A single bar on a 0–0.5 scale with the gate's effective ceiling marked; median 0.015, p90 0.109, max 0.400, and zero passing edges above 0.5.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv frac_co_ZNF
interactions: hover → 'the KRAB-ZNF expansion is one clade counted hundreds of times; 547 ZNF genes contribute an effective sample size of 9.0'
link to the artifact explainer
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is one number that pre-empts the first objection any reviewer will raise, and putting it inline on every edge rather than behind a toggle is what makes the caveat structural.

units.name: Edge inspector — UMAP locator
units.what_it_shows: Where this specific edge sits in the 180,000-pair embedding.
units.encoding: A 160×160 thumbnail of the pair UMAP with all pairs at 8% opacity, the 2,620 gated pairs lit, and this pair marked.
units.data_source: cca_winner_umap.npy + row_index.csv joined on (protein, utr)
interactions: click → the full pair explorer with this point selected
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It ties the network's local view back to the global one for a reader who wants to know whether this edge is typical of its neighbourhood.

units.name: Edge inspector — carrier sequence preview strip
units.what_it_shows: For three or four carrier genes, the actual local sequence around each matched motif on both sides — the manuscript's Fig 4a idiom, inside the edge panel.
units.encoding: Monospace rows, motif upper-case and tinted, flanks lower-case grey, motif starting at a fixed column; UTR shown in RNA alphabet.
units.data_source: GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet sequences sliced with the verified inclusive rule seq[motif_start:motif_end+1]; coordinates from motif_full_annotations.parquet; ordering logic portable from examples_of_each_gene/examples_lib.py context()
interactions: click a row → the R1 transcript view at that position
cycle to the next carriers
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the moment where an abstract edge becomes two real sequences in a real gene. Nothing else in R3 does that, and the slicing contract is already verified exact over all 889,215 rows.

units.name: Module panel — GO dot plot with trusted toggle
units.what_it_shows: The module's GO themes, defaulting to the authors' stricter 'trusted' subset (q<0.05 AND fold≥2 AND n_fam_support≥5).
units.encoding: Dots: x = fold, y = term, size = n_genes, colour = −log10 q, with a companion bar per row for n_fam_support so a term resting on one expanded paralog family is visible as such. Both counts printed on the toggle: M1 1,419 of 2,310, M2 442/962, M3 383/926, M4 223/342, M5 593/1,086, M6 470/763.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v4_0621/03.interacting_modules/module_GO_enrichment.csv (6,389 rows already filtered to q<0.05; columns module_id, term, name, k, K, n_query, fold, p, n_fam_support, dom_family_frac, q, n_genes)
interactions: trusted/all toggle
hover → full contingency plus dom_family_frac
click a term → the genes driving it
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Module GO themes are how the six modules got their names, and the report explicitly warns not to read raw counts of significant terms. n_fam_support on every row is what makes that warning actionable.

units.name: Module panel — GO specificity slope chart
units.what_it_shows: Which terms actually discriminate this module from the other five: peak module −log10 q against the runner-up, for the 42 representative terms (38 with a gap ≥ 5 log units).
units.encoding: Slope lines from peak_nlq to second_nlq, sorted by specificity_gap, coloured by peak module.
units.data_source: 03.interacting_modules/GO_term_specificity.csv (42 rows: term, peak_module, peak_nlq, second_nlq, specificity_gap, n_modules_sig), with GO_terms_module_specific.csv (38) and GO_terms_shared_across_modules.csv (3)
interactions: hover → both q values and the runner-up module
click → that term across all six modules
units.why_it_earns_its_place: M1 and M2 are both TF modules with heavily overlapping GO; the specificity gap is the only honest way to say what separates them, and the file is 2.5 KB and already computed.

units.name: Module panel — member gene table
units.what_it_shows: The genes that carry both motifs of at least one gated pair of this module, with their GO hit counts and paralog families.
units.encoding: Virtualised table: gene, n_transcripts, paralog_families, n_sig_terms_hit, n_trusted_terms_hit; the trusted_terms cell rendered as a count with an expander, never as the raw semicolon string (NOTCH1 holds 268 terms).
units.data_source: 03.interacting_modules/module_gene_members/module_gene_index.csv (12,345 rows; per module 3,083 / 2,434 / 3,112 / 844 / 1,482 / 1,390 genes hitting ≥1 significant term)
interactions: search, sort, export
row → R1 transcript view via refseq_ids
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 'Representative genes' is part of the requirement, and this is the only file that connects modules to gene symbols with a verified refseq join.

units.name: Module panel — membership definition note
units.what_it_shows: That a module gene is one carrying BOTH motifs of at least one gated pair, and that the table's row count (genes hitting ≥1 significant term) is smaller than total membership (M1 3,083 vs 3,388).
units.encoding: One explanatory line above the table with both numbers.
units.data_source: 03.interacting_modules/module_gene_members/README.md, quoted verbatim
interactions: link to the methods page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Two different gene counts per module circulate in these files. Printing both with their definitions prevents a reader deriving a contradiction and concluding the portal is unreliable.

units.name: Module panel — representative pair chips
units.what_it_shows: The five pre-selected representative interactions per module, already chosen upstream.
units.encoding: Chips formatted 'prot_0040 × utr5_0004', each with its score.
units.data_source: modules.json top_pairs[] (e.g. M6: prot_0040xutr5_0004, prot_0040xutr3_0463, prot_0235xutr5_0004, prot_0030xutr3_0463, prot_0235xutr3_0463; M3: five pairs all involving utr5_0090)
interactions: click → edge inspector with that edge selected in the canvas
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Free, already curated, and it gives every module a guaranteed non-empty entry point. M3's five top pairs all sharing utr5_0090 is itself a visible result.

units.name: Module panel — member cluster gallery
units.what_it_shows: Every cluster in the module (not the ≤5-per-side figure cap) as a card with logo, name and degree.
units.encoding: Two-column card grid, protein left, UTR right; card border in the region colour; M3 shows all 62+71.
units.data_source: modules.json member lists + consensus_meta.csv + the per-cluster index
interactions: click → node inspector
sort by degree, n_genes or consensus coverage
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The published figure shows 52 of 513 module clusters. A reader who assumes the figure is the module will be wrong by an order of magnitude, and the gallery is the correction.

units.name: Module panel — cross-module link bars
units.what_it_shows: This module's connections to the other five with counts and mean scores.
units.encoding: Horizontal bars in the partner module's colour: for M5 → M1 192 (mean 0.325), M2 28, M6 15, M3 5, M4 4.
units.data_source: the derived 6×6 adjacency
interactions: click → the canvas filtered to that module pair
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It puts the manuscript's own M5–M1 observation on the M5 page, where a reader looking at M5 will actually find it.

units.name: Gate definition card
units.what_it_shows: The four conditions and the edge-weight formula, quoted exactly, wherever a gate value appears.
units.encoding: A compact card: clade_concentration < 0.35 AND n_indep_clades ≥ 8 AND npmi_mip_APC > 0.10 AND co_count ≥ 10; weight = MIp × (1 − clade_concentration) × log1p(n_indep_clades); Louvain modularity 0.47, 9 communities, 6 retained.
units.data_source: 03.interacting_modules/MODULES_REPORT.md, verbatim
interactions: open from any gate gauge
links to the funnel
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Every number in this view depends on these four inequalities. They should be one hover away from every place they are applied.

units.name: Association funnel
units.what_it_shows: 180,000 scored pairs → 166,615 co-occurring → 2,620 gated (1.6%).
units.encoding: Three nested horizontal bars drawn to scale, each labelled with the condition that removed the difference; the final bar is a sliver, which is the point.
units.data_source: results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (180,000 rows; 13,385 with co_count 0; 166,615 with co_count > 0; 2,620 with passes_phylo_filter)
interactions: hover a stage → per-condition removal counts
click → the pair explorer filtered to that population
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the honest scale statement for the whole view, and it belongs in R3's chrome rather than only on a methods page — the network is what survived, and the reader should know how little that is.

units.name: Raw-vs-corrected artifact toggle
units.what_it_shows: Sorting the top 30 pairs by raw NPMI yields 25 'ZNF clade artifact' verdicts; re-sorting by the corrected score replaces them.
units.encoding: A table with a sort toggle; artifact rows tinted vermillion, 'survives' tinted teal; the reordering animates so the artifacts visibly fall away. Row 1 raw is prot_0228 × utr5_0020, npmi_raw 0.8969, 2 clades, frac_co_ZNF 0.990, passes_phylo_filter False.
units.data_source: results/RAW_top30_annotated.csv (30 rows × 16 columns including a hand-written verdict column: 25 / 4 / 1)
interactions: toggle the sort key
click any row → the pair detail, including rejected pairs which open with a REJECTED banner and the failing gate highlighted
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the most persuasive artifact in the entire project and it needs no new writing. Reachable from the network's caveat bar, it converts the mandatory disclaimer into a demonstration.

units.name: Effective sample size bars
units.what_it_shows: Why paralogy needed correcting: 18,068 genes have an effective sample size of 2,342 (13.0%); the 547 ZNF genes contribute an effective 9.0 (1.7%).
units.encoding: Two paired bars on a shared linear scale so the collapse is literal, with the ratio printed.
units.data_source: results/relatedness_report.md
interactions: hover → the verbatim sentence from the report
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the single arithmetic fact that justifies every gate threshold, and it takes two bars.

units.name: Persistent co-occurrence caveat bar
units.what_it_shows: That edges are statistical co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes, not demonstrated physical interaction — as non-dismissible chrome on this view specifically.
units.encoding: A 40 px band, warn tint, one sentence plus a 'why?' link; not collapsible on the network, module or edge views.
units.data_source: quoted verbatim from 03.interacting_modules/module_gene_members/README.md and MODULES_REPORT.md
interactions: 'why?' → the artifact explainer
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A bipartite graph with thick edges is read as an interactome. The data model should also name the field 'co-occurrence' so no template can ever emit 'binds'.

units.name: Network legend / encoding key
units.what_it_shows: All simultaneous encodings with live example glyphs: shape = region, fill = module, area = carrier genes, width = phylo score, solid/dashed = consensus tier, light stroke = cross-module.
units.encoding: A compact always-visible block drawn by the same code as the canvas, so it can never drift from what is rendered.
units.data_source: the palette constants in _shared/manuscript_style.py and the MCOL mapping used identically by four published figure scripts (M1 #0072B2, M2 #CC79A7, M3 #E69F00, M4 #D55E00, M5 #4D4D4D, M6 #009E73)
interactions: click a module swatch → isolate that module
click the dashed key → highlight all consensus-less edges
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Five simultaneous channels is at the edge of what a reader can hold; a legend drawn by the rendering code is the only way to keep it honest. Note that three conflicting module palettes exist in the codebase — pick MCOL and say so.

units.name: Selection breadcrumb
units.what_it_shows: Where the reader is in the meta → module → node/edge hierarchy and what is currently pinned.
units.encoding: Chips: 'Network / M5 / prot_0072 × utr5_0079', each dismissable, with a neighbour count when a node is selected.
units.data_source: view state
interactions: each chip navigates up a level
'pin' keeps a selection while exploring another
units.why_it_earns_its_place: With three zoom levels and two inspector types it is easy to lose track of what the panel is describing.

units.name: Pin-and-compare tray
units.what_it_shows: Two or three pinned nodes or edges side by side for direct comparison.
units.encoding: A bottom tray of pinned cards; comparing two edges shows their gate gauges on shared axes so the values are directly readable against each other.
units.data_source: the same records as the inspectors
interactions: pin from any inspector; unpin; swap into the main panel
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The natural question after opening one edge is 'is this better than that one', and switching panels loses the first set of numbers.

units.name: Empty-state cards (four kinds)
units.what_it_shows: Four distinct absences, each explained with its measured number: (a) this cluster has no gated partner (282 of 600 UTR and 99 of 300 protein clusters); (b) this cluster is in no module (387 of 900: 102 protein, 251 utr3, 34 utr5); (c) this node has no significant STREME motif (68 of 519 network nodes); (d) this node has no term at FDR<0.05 (211 of 519).
units.encoding: Bordered cards with the cause, the count, and one onward action — never a blank panel.
units.data_source: derived flags over modules.json, consensus_repertoire.pkl, cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz and protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv
interactions: (a) offers the sub-threshold ghost edges; (b) links to the gate explainer; (c) offers the member-string fallback; (d) offers the instance-frequency bars
units.why_it_earns_its_place: These four states cover a large fraction of all possible clicks. Treated generically they read as bugs; treated specifically they are four of the portal's most informative screens.

units.name: Loading skeletons
units.what_it_shows: That a panel or the canvas is loading, in the shape of what will arrive.
units.encoding: Shape-matched shimmer blocks for the canvas, the inspector and the logo slots, so nothing jumps on arrival.
units.data_source: n/a

layout_options.name: A. Fig 3e-faithful two-column bipartite with sticky inspector
layout_options.pros: Reproduces the printed Fig 3e arrangement, so a reader arriving from the paper recognises it immediately. Protein-left/UTR-right makes the bilingual claim structural rather than decorative. Node glyphs carry the logo AND the positional histogram exactly as published, which is what the requirement asks for. Module bands give a stable vertical ordering that makes cross-module edges literally longer than intra-module ones, so the 28.9% cross-linking is visible without a special mode. The sticky inspector never moves the graph.
layout_options.cons: At 519 nodes the two columns are ~250 nodes tall each, so it is a scrolling or heavily zoomed canvas; node glyphs with logos only fit at high zoom, so labels and logos must appear via semantic zoom. Hub nodes (prot_0223 at degree 62) still produce local clutter, requiring the degree cap. The vertical module ordering can only place adjacent modules adjacently, so some cross-module edges span the whole canvas.
layout_options.best_for: The manuscript reader and the reviewer — anyone whose mental model is Fig 3e and who wants to check specific published pairs. Also the best default for a first-time visitor arriving from the paper's URL, provided it opens on the 52-node 'as published' preset rather than all 519.

layout_options.name: B. Level-of-detail cockpit: persistent meta rail + main canvas + inspector
layout_options.pros: The 6x6 module matrix stays on screen at all times, so the reader never loses global context while drilling — and because it is a matrix rather than a node-link, it preserves the directional asymmetry (M1p->M2u 178 vs M2p->M1u 66) that a symmetric meta graph destroys. The main canvas only ever draws one module (max 133 nodes, M3), so a hairball is structurally impossible in the default path. The partner rail below the canvas turns a degree-62 hub from an unreadable star into a sortable strip. Drill-down is one click and the way back is always visible.
layout_options.cons: Costs ~280px of permanent horizontal real estate to the rail. The full 519-node graph becomes a secondary mode rather than the default, which some readers will want. Requires the reader to understand a matrix, which is a small but real cognitive cost. Cross-module edges are shown as stubs in the default module view rather than as complete edges, so following one takes an extra click.
layout_options.best_for: The browsing scientist working through the six modules systematically — the reader who asks 'what is M5 and how does it connect to M1' rather than 'show me everything'. Also the best layout for a laptop screen, because it never needs more than ~130 nodes on the canvas at once.

layout_options.name: C. Matrix-first: seriated adjacency heatmap with linked marginals
layout_options.pros: Cannot hairball, by construction. Every pair is addressable in constant time, so 'is prot_0040 linked to utr3_0463?' is answered by looking at one cell instead of tracing a curve. Module blocks appear as dense diagonal squares and their densities become directly comparable (M1 0.296 vs M3 0.087) — a real result that no node-link layout conveys. Off-diagonal spatter IS the cross-module story, at full resolution, with no toggle needed. Marginal degree bars replace a separate degree chart. Switching the encoded quantity (score / npmi / co_count / clades / ZNF) reuses the identical geometry, so the reader compares like with like. Backed directly by results/corrected_score_matrices.npz with no reshaping.
layout_options.cons: Paths are invisible — 'what is prot_0072 connected to, transitively' is unanswerable. Requires a good seriation or it looks like noise. Row and column labels for 201+318 nodes cannot all be shown, so labels must be on hover or on a zoomed sub-block. Least familiar representation for a bench biologist; needs a short explainer. Empty cells must be captioned 'no gated edge' or they will be read as 'no evidence', which is wrong — most of them merely failed the gate.
layout_options.best_for: The sceptical or systematic reader: a reviewer checking whether the module block structure is real, a bioinformatician looking for a specific pair, or anyone comparing modules quantitatively. Also the best printable representation, and the right default if the audience is expected to arrive with a specific hypothesis rather than to browse.

layout_options.name: D. Six-panel small-multiples module atlas with shared inspector
layout_options.pros: Comparison is the design, not a mode. All six modules fit on one laptop screen because the largest (M3) is 133 nodes and the smallest (M6) is 32. Identical node-size and edge-width scales across panels make the density differences (0.087 to 0.296) and the size differences (774 vs 43 edges) directly readable — these are real results that a single interactive canvas hides behind toggles. Each panel carries its theme caption and ZNF risk, so the six modules become six characterised objects rather than six colours. It is also the most print- and slide-friendly arrangement.
layout_options.cons: Individual nodes are too small to carry a logo or a positional histogram, so the Fig 3e glyph requirement must be met elsewhere (hover, or on drill-down). Cross-module edges cannot be drawn as real edges and degrade to stubs plus the summary line at the bottom, which under-represents 28.9% of the result. Reading a specific pair requires drilling in. Six force layouts must each be frozen and kept stable.
layout_options.best_for: The reader comparing modules — someone deciding which module is relevant to their gene, or a talk audience seeing the six-module result for the first time. Works best as the landing state of R3 with any of layouts A/B/C as the drill-down destination.

layout_options.name: E. Split-screen dual representation with brushed linking
layout_options.pros: Every alternative representation earns its place without competing for the same screen — the reader chooses two at a time and they are brushed-linked, so a cluster of points in the UMAP lights up as a subgraph and vice versa. The raw-vs-corrected scatter can sit on the right while the node-link sits on the left, which makes the artifact argument visible AND spatial. The selection table below is the accessible, exportable, sortable equivalent of whatever is drawn above, so nothing is image-only. Naturally accommodates the arc, Sankey, matrix and small-multiples units as pane options rather than as separate pages.
layout_options.cons: Two panes on a laptop means each is roughly 700px wide — too narrow for node glyphs carrying logos, so this layout cannot satisfy the 'node glyph with consensus logo' part of the requirement on its own. Brushing across two different embeddings needs careful explanation or it implies the two spaces are comparable, which they are not. More UI machinery than the other layouts and the most opportunity for a reader to end up in a combination that makes no sense.
layout_options.best_for: The analyst — someone interrogating the result rather than reading it: checking whether the gated pairs occupy a distinct region of the UMAP, whether high-ZNF pairs cluster, or whether one module's edges are systematically weaker. Best offered as a secondary 'explore' mode reachable from A, B or C, not as the landing view.

open_questions: BLOCKING, and it lands squarely on this view: the manuscript's only named M2 example says 'MLXIPL … contains the M2 utr3_0027 motifs', but modules.json assigns utr3_0027 to M1 while the code that produced Fig 4a (build_mlxipl_signatures.py, MLXIPL_M2_signatures.csv) uses utr3_0227, which is M2. utr3_0227 is also a degree-37 UTR hub in the network. Whichever way the M2 module card and node label are built, the portal will expose the inconsistency. One question to the author; build on utr3_0227 in the meantime.

Which module palette is canonical? Three conflicting mappings exist: the MCOL used identically by four published figure scripts (M1 #0072B2, M2 #CC79A7, M3 #E69F00, M4 #D55E00, M5 #4D4D4D, M6 #009E73), the CATEGORICAL cycle in motif_umap/make_individual_figures.py (M1 gray, M2 blue, M3 orange, M4 teal, M5 purple, M6 sky blue), and an unimplemented proposal in _shared/COLOR_TABLE.md. I recommend MCOL because Fig 3d/3e/ED3b use it, but then any embedded Fig 3c UMAP image will disagree unless recoloured at bake time. Confirm before the legend is written.

Should the 757 cross-module edges get consensus-pair scores? Zero of them have one today because 17_consensus_association.py was only run within modules, and the M1-M5 block (192 edges, the highest mean cross score at 0.325) is the manuscript's own headline cross-module observation. consensus_presence.npz makes the computation a bitwise AND, but nobody has measured the runtime or decided whether the results are publishable. This is the single highest-value new computation for R3.

Is the STREME gap-fill in scope before the node glyph is designed? 68 of the 519 network nodes have no significant PWM. Running the 387 never-run clusters is reportedly ~15 min at WORKERS=10 with the binary at /Users/wangyanz/software/meme/bin/streme, but roughly 100-150 protein clusters are expected to return nothing even after running. The layout should be designed against the coverage it will actually have, not retrofitted.

What is the default landing state of R3? I would open on the 52-node 'as published' preset (113 edges, density 0.167, 40 of them cross-module) so a reader from the paper recognises it, with a one-click expansion to all 519. But that means the landing view shows 4.3% of the edges. Confirm the author is comfortable with a curated default, or switch to the six-panel module atlas.

Should the relaxed tier (npmi_mip_APC > 0.10, 7,210 edges over 835 nodes, 4,590 of which fail the gate) be reachable from the network view at all, or only from a cluster's partner table? Enabling it on the canvas nearly triples the edges and adds 316 nodes, which is a genuine hairball. My recommendation is to allow it only in ego/module scope, never in the full canvas.

Is a live-force 'nudge' mode wanted alongside the frozen layout? Frozen positions are required for deep links and reproducibility, but readers will want to untangle local regions. If yes, the reset must be prominent and the URL must record which mode produced the picture.

No cross-reference exists from the 1,226 discovered consensus to any known RBP motif database (CISBP-RNA, RBPmap, ATtRACT, Ray et al.) anywhere in the trees. So a node labelled UCUCC cannot answer 'is that the PTBP motif?', and the manuscript's own SRSF3/4 and PTBP attributions for utr5_0096 and utr3_0215 have no enrichment row in the data. Should those be badged as 'author inference from literature' distinct from 'evidence in this dataset'? TOMTOM ships with the same MEME install and could close this later.

Which quantity should be the default edge encoding — phylo_corrected_score (the layout weight, range 0.146-1.769) or npmi_mip_APC (the association strength, 0.100-0.721)? They are correlated but not identical, since the score multiplies in (1 - clade_concentration) and log1p(n_indep_clades). I default to phylo_corrected_score for width because it is what the modules were built from, but a reader thinking in terms of association strength may expect NPMI.

Should sub-threshold ghost edges be available globally or only per-selection? Globally they would show the reader the full evidence landscape (58,204 pairs have npmi_mip_APC > 0), but they would also make the canvas unreadable and risk being screenshotted out of context. I have specified per-selection only; confirm.

The pair UMAP coordinates live in sequence_analysis_v3_0515, a tree that nothing in the v4 pipeline references or regenerates, and they cannot be recomputed to match the published figure. If the UMAP pane is built, the file must be copied into a versioned snapshot with its mtime and SHA-256 recorded. Confirm no newer version exists.

Should the three unassigned-endpoint edges (prot_0291 x utr5_0013, prot_0108 x utr3_0355, prot_0058 x utr3_0139) be drawn in the main canvas as isolated dyads, or moved to a small 'ungrouped pairs' tray? They are real gated edges but they float outside the giant component and will look like a rendering error.
